newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Santista says in talks to buy soy operation.
newsitem.headline: Santista says in talks to buy soy operation.

text.p: Brazilian food processor Santista Alimentos said it told the Securities and Exchange Commission (CVM) and the local stock exchanges it was in talks to buy a soybean crushing facility from Incobrasa.

"Santista informed the CVM and the Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro bourses in a letter it is in negotiations with the controllers of Incobrasa and is interested in buying its soybean crushing business in Rio Grande do Sul," a spokeswoman said.
Financial daily Gazeta Mercantil reported Wednesday that Santista, a subsidiary of Bunge y Born, had bought Incobrasa's soybean operation for an estimated $80 million.
The deal was said to include two soybean crushers with a joint capacity of 5,500 tonnes per day, three silos and Incobrasa's private terminal at the port of Rio Grande.
